A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CES research work and contain complete main text and Appendices A–D. Text extraction and rendered-page checks support comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original temporal-ordering experiments, CES benchmark results, component ablations, training curves, model-scaling analyses, and a GUI task case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 3 and 5 and Appendices B and D, although some baseline scores remain explicitly attributed to earlier work.

M1.justification: The CES loop, frozen Executor, warm-up SFT, staged GRPO optimization, and reward functions remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix A. Revised vision-language/language-model terminology does not change the specified models or procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use GUI-Odyssey training data and evaluate on AITZ, AMEX, and GUI-Odyssey. The temporal-ordering scenario and the appendix's Zoom–Tumblr–Clock case study are also retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain identical comparator membership, including SWIRL, GPT-5 prompting, and the Baseline/CES-P/CES comparisons using UI-R1-3B, GUI-Owl-7B, and GUI-Owl-32B.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same model configurations, 1K SFT and 3K RL training samples, training budgets, and Type/GR/SR evaluation definitions. No experimental protocol or setting is revised.

E4.justification: The temporal-ordering experiment, component and RL ablations, failure analysis, training curves, model-scaling analysis, and detailed case study are unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the same result tables and training/scaling plots are retained.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative case findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains GUI-R1-7B + CES SR values of 43.05%, 48.48%, and 53.69% on AITZ, AMEX, and GUI-Odyssey, respectively.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation and Equations 1–25 retain the same mathematical content, including Appendix A's optimization objectives and reward definitions. Apparent extraction differences in v2's equations do not represent mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: decoupled high-level scheduling, a dedicated State Tracker, staged execution-feedback RL, and generalizable improvements across Executor models.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning capability conflicts, task-state awareness, model capacity, and the remaining Executor perception bottleneck are substantively unchanged. Appendix D retains the same explanations of planning and grounding failures.

D1.justification: The abstract changes 'Code can be available' to 'Code is available' at the same repository address, making the availability declaration explicit. Implementation settings and prompts are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an actual repository-status change.

R1.justification: The same 48 references and the same research positioning in Section 2 are retained. References shift across pages following the added acknowledgment, without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 corrects scattered grammar, spelling, punctuation, and model-name capitalization; renames Section 4.1 from 'Preliminary' to 'Task Setup'; updates affiliation and author footnotes; and adds a funding acknowledgment. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1's caption changes 'High-level task' to 'Long-horizon task,' and Figure 2's caption receives a punctuation correction. Added front matter and the acknowledgment cause local reflow; all figures and tables retain their visual content and structure.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves readability through copyediting, the clearer 'Task Setup' heading, and more precise Table 1 terminology. It also clarifies the code-availability declaration. The gains are limited to clarity and reporting: the scientific methods, empirical support, and appendix analyses remain unchanged, and an actual code release cannot be verified from the PDFs.
